title: Scale, Extend, or Stop?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Apply a pilot decision rule to six pilot results and judge whether each pilot should scale, extend, or stop.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each of six pilot results leads to scaling, extending, or stopping by applying the stated decision rule, correctly judging at least five of six on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Pilot program, pilot goals, and decision rule, from the section "Readiness and Pilots" in Chapter 20.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify one item at a time with immediate feedback; first-attempt scoring
keyQuestions: Are all three scale conditions met?
commonMisconceptions: A high test gain is enough to scale.
A pilot that misses one goal has failed.
A privacy incident can be offset by learning gains.
assessmentOpportunities: Gain 0.30 SD with a serious privacy incident. What does the rule say?
Gain 0.16 SD, workload +2 hours, satisfaction 65 percent. What does the rule say?
Does a pilot that misses one goal fail?

controls.name: Category buttons
controls.description: Choose the decision for the current pilot result.

controls.name: Submit
controls.description: Checks the choice. Two tries per pilot result; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next pilot result. Finish shows the score.

controls.name: Start over
controls.description: Reshuffles and begins a new run.
